descriptionAdvanced.en: Valparaíso is a legendary port city built on a natural amphitheater of 42 steep hills overlooking the Pacific Ocean. Known for its chaotic yet beautiful arrangement of colorful houses, winding staircases, and historic funiculars, it has long inspired artists and writers like Pablo Neruda. The city's historic quarter is a UNESCO World Heritage site, celebrated for its unique 19th-century urban design and architecture. As the seat of the Chilean National Congress, it remains a vital political center while maintaining its bohemian and gritty charm. Its vibrant street art scene makes every corner of the city feel like an open-air gallery.

en: Declared a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2003 for its cultural and architectural value.
Home to 'La Sebastiana,' one of the three houses of Nobel Prize-winning poet Pablo Neruda.
Features a system of historic funicular elevators, some dating back to the late 19th century.
Serves as the headquarters of the Chilean Navy and the National Congress.
Historically known as the 'Jewel of the Pacific' during its golden age before the Panama Canal.
